body: This is one of the important open questions. If it isn’t present, the tailscale client won’t let you use `--ssh`. However, I don’t know what else it enables or if it should be included only for certain users.
In the error case we leave action in the reject state and continue processing the rule. Perhaps it would be better to continue to the next rule instead?
We should make similar constructor functions for the accept and reject actions as well.

Something like this?
```go
var action tailcfg.SSHAction

switch sshACL.Action {
case "accept":
	action = sshAcceptAction()
case "check":
	checkAction, err := sshCheckAction(sshACL.CheckPeriod)
	if err != nil {
		log.Error().
			Msgf("Error parsing SSH %d, check action with unparsable duration '%s'", index, sshACL.CheckPeriod)
	} else {
		action = *checkAction
	}
	fallthrough
default:
	action = sshRejectAction()

	log.Error().
		Msgf("Error parsing SSH %d, unknown action '%s'", index, sshACL.Action)

	return nil, err
}
```
No, that fallthrough is wrong. There needs to be a case for `"reject"` as well.

From my understanding of [the docs](https://tailscale.com/kb/1193/tailscale-ssh/#ensure-tailscale-ssh-is-permitted-in-acls), only `accept` or `check` is valid. Happy to be proven wrong as I haven't read all the available documentation :-)
